newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria, Kuwait discuss economic cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Syria, Kuwait discuss economic cooperation.

text.p: Kuwaiti and Syrian officials met in Damascus on Monday to discuss economic cooperation including expanding trade and setting up a joint airline.

Mustafa Shmali, assistant underscretary at the Kuwaiti Finance Ministry, said the meeting would discuss among other things financing of communications and industrial projects in Syria by Kuwait's Development Fund, the establishment of a joint airline and a customs agreement to eliminate double taxation.
Kuwait is seeking to expand trade with syria and adjust the balance which is in Syria's favour, he told Reuters.
Economic sources said exports of Syrian light manufactured products, vegetables and fruits accounted for the bulk of the $85 million annual two-way trade between Kuwait and Syria.
Kuwait wants to export petrochemicals and oil products to Syria, the sources said.
Monday's meeting was the fifth session of the Syria-Kuwaiti Cooperation Committee, which meets once every six months in Kuwait or Damascus.

Shortly after the meeting opened, the Kuwaiti delegation joined Syrian Prime Minister Mahmoud Zu'bi in inaugurating the 384-megawatt Nassiriah power station north of Damascus. Kuwait's Development Fund contributed $132 million of the $158 million cost of the plant, officials said.
Until September, the fund had given Syria soft loans totalling $884 million to finance several development projects, officials said.
Shmali said a recently established $200 million Kuwaiti investment company, the first fully-owned foreign company in Syria, would start its activities in early 1997.
Kuwait's Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan and Syrian Deputy Prime Minister for economic affairs Salim Yassin head the two delegations at the talks.
